prompt: What is a milestone, by the lesson?

choices.text: A percentage of the work finished, reported every week
The date on which the whole project must be over
A long document describing the next phase of the project
choices.why: It ends in something that runs.

choices.text: A state you could demonstrate, with a date

prompt: Match each loanbook tag to what could be shown at it.

pairs.right: List, lend and take back, end to end
A second loan refused; late loans marked
The page at an address, over HTTPS

prompt: Which properties make loanbook's milestones good ones? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Each one is demonstrable
Each one is useful on its own
They are few
They are evenly spaced
choices.why: The gaps are uneven, and that is normal.

prompt: Why is the one thing in the first milestone after the skeleton?

choices.text: Because it was the easiest part of the project to build
So the point is done whatever happens later
Because git tags need a rule in them
Because Marta asked for it first

prompt: How many milestones did loanbook have?
An annotated tag is made with git tag ___ and listed with its message by git tag ___.
What does a major version of 0, as in v0.2.0, say?

choices.text: Not yet worth showing
It has no code in it yet
It was released by mistake
It is the second version of the project

prompt: A project tags its first commit v1.0.0. What does the lesson say about that?

choices.text: Git refuses a tag on a first commit
Semantic versioning forbids starting at one
It spent the word early
Nothing, the number means nothing to anybody
choices.why: It means something to a reviewer.

prompt: In the capture, how many files changed between v0.2.0 and v0.3.0?
hint: The last line of the stat.

prompt: Which question does git diff --stat v0.2.0 v0.3.0 answer?

choices.text: What did the deploy milestone cost?
Who wrote each line of the project?
Which tests failed on the server?
When was the project first deployed?

prompt: Which command sends the tags to GitHub or GitLab?

choices.text: git push --tags
git tag --push
git commit --tags
git release

prompt: Which make a self-set deadline hold, by the lesson? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Say it to somebody
A date on each milestone, not only the end
Decide in advance what happens when you miss one
Keep the date secret, so nobody is disappointed

prompt: You miss a milestone. What does the lesson say to do?

choices.text: Move every later date by the same amount
Start over from the skeleton with a new plan
Cut, don't extend
Drop the one thing to catch up

prompt: Why does moving the date turn six weeks into six months, by the lesson?

choices.text: Hosting prices rise after six weeks
The second move is easier than the first
Git history grows too long to read
Reviewers reject late projects

prompt: What does telling somebody the date do, by the lesson?

choices.text: Obliges them to review the code on that day
choices.why: You are not asking anybody to check.

choices.text: Makes the date legally binding
Lets them move it for you
Makes moving it slightly embarrassing, without asking anyone to check

prompt: Put the weekly note's lines in the order the example uses.
What counts as shipped in the weekly note?

choices.text: Tasks started this week, finished or not
Hours spent on the project
Every commit, however small
What runs now and did not last week

prompt: What does the lesson say about the worry line?

choices.text: It should be left out, since it spreads anxiety
Named early it is a task; found late, a missed milestone
It is the only line a reviewer reads
It replaces the next line

prompt: Why write the notes weekly rather than from memory at the end?
hint: What happened or what you wish had.

choices.text: Git deletes notes older than a month
They record what happened, not what you wished
Reviewers check the dates on every note
Weekly notes are shorter to write

prompt: A student's plan says: milestone 1, 40% done; milestone 2, 80% done; milestone 3, finished. What is wrong with it?

choices.text: Nothing runs at the first two
choices.why: Right. Name what runs at each.

choices.text: There should be exactly four milestones
choices.why: The count is not the problem.

choices.text: The percentages are too optimistic for a junior
choices.why: The problem is that they are percentages.

choices.text: Milestones should not have numbers

prompt: Week 4: the deploy milestone is a week late and the search box is half done. What does the lesson's reasoning say?

choices.text: Move the final date by a week
Finish the search box first, it is half done
choices.why: Half done is not a reason.

choices.text: Drop the extra that is half built
Skip the deploy and tag v1.0.0
